hypothesis: On a cold start the baseline downloads the 1,981 MiB Q8_0 GGUF into a memfd (25.0 s p50) and only then lets llama.cpp load it (model_load_mmap 8.4 s p50, which includes KleidiAI repacking each Q8_0 matmul weight as it reads it). The loader reads the header first and then each tensor once, so the load can start as soon as the header is present and repack each tensor as its bytes land. Overlapping the two should cut cold download+load towards max(download, load), change no output, and leave a SnapStart restore (which never downloads or loads) unchanged, provided the overlap leaves the same process memory behind. Run 1 showed it did not (+470 MB of glibc thread-arena retention); run 2 pins glibc's mmap threshold so the arenas cannot grow.

changed_variable.name: download/load overlap
changed_variable.baseline: download_to_memfd completes, then llama_model_load_from_file mmaps the memfd (P1)
changed_variable.experiment: llama_model_load_from_file starts once the GGUF header is in the memfd; a dormant llama.cpp hook (e4_stream/patch_stream.py) blocks each tensor's read until its bytes have arrived and loads tensors in expected-arrival order; glibc's mmap threshold is pinned at 4 MiB (mallopt M_MMAP_THRESHOLD) so the overlapped repack cannot make the download threads' arenas retain memory (arm stream). Same file, same download (HEAD + 31 x 64 MiB ranges on 32 threads, 8 MiB reads), same mmap path and kernels. Controls: basethr = base with the pin only; streamdyn = the overlap without the pin (run 1's stream arm)

conclusion: Run 2 of 2 (arms base / stream / basethr / streamdyn, 5 rounds x 10 per class, interleaved; 0 errors, 0 class mismatches; 2,400 of 2,400 answers bit-identical to P1's reference). stream vs base, within CPU part: cold first-request -4.54 s on CPU part 0xd40 (35.92 -> 31.38 s p50, -13 %), -3.97 s on CPU part 0xd4f (-12 %, 4 samples), -9.26 s on CPU part 0xd0c (48.49 -> 39.23 s, -19 %), -5.64 s pooled; download+load -5.64 s pooled (33.71 -> 29.16 s p50) with the download itself unchanged; restore first-request -0.02 s (3.93 -> 3.92 s p50; per-round medians overlap, i.e. no change); Max Memory Used -34 MB cold, -41 MB restore, -59 MB warm; steady-state inference -0.02 s (noise). The pin alone (basethr) changes cold by +0.19 s and memory by -35 to -58 MB, so the cold gain is the overlap's and the memory recovery is the pin's. streamdyn reproduces run 1: cold -5.50 s but restore +0.34 s and memory +476 to +495 MB, confirming the restore regression was memory, not the overlap. SnapStart: the download and load run inside publish_version's snapshot init, never in a restore, so SnapStart already hides E4's cold-path saving on restore; E4 improves on-demand cold starts (and shortens the snapshot init), and with the pin leaves restore unchanged. Host variability: comparisons are within CPU part and every round agrees in sign (host_variability); no Graviton generation is claimed, and no rerun was needed.

host_assessment: Comparable; no rerun. Observed per request: cpuinfo CPU part (0xd40, 0xd0c, 0xd4f drawn); per cold environment the ggml CPU variants loaded (0xd40 armv8.6_1, 0xd0c armv8.2_2, 0xd4f armv8.6_2, one variant set per part) and threads=6 (the handler's os.cpu_count(); THREADS unset); one runtime (python:3.12.mainlinev2.v43, same ARN) on all 241 INIT_START streams; 10,240 MB arm64. Not recorded by either run, so unknown: cpuinfo implementer/variant/revision, Features flags, AT_HWCAP/HWCAP2, cgroup limits, kernel release, AZ and physical host. No Graviton generation is claimed: the runs recorded only the CPU part number. Why the host mix cannot change the conclusions: every arm-vs-base delta is taken within one CPU part, arms are interleaved in each round, and every round's within-part delta has the same sign for each conclusion (host_variability.per_round_deltas). stream cold first-request: 0xd40 -4.31 to -4.75 s over 5 rounds, 0xd0c -7.50 to -9.52 s over 5 rounds, 0xd4f -3.94 s in the 1 round both arms drew it. stream restore on 0xd40: -0.05 to +0.06 s (mixed sign, i.e. no effect); memory -36 to -44 MB in every round and part. streamdyn restore +0.32 to +0.42 s and memory +466 to +510 MB in every round. Limits: the parts are drawn unevenly across arms (cold 0xd40: base 27, stream 36, basethr 42, streamdyn 29 of 50), so the unsplit per-arm distributions in phases mix parts and are not comparable across arms; use <arm>_vs_base.by_cpu_part. No restore landed on 0xd4f, so restore conclusions cover 0xd40 and 0xd0c only; 0xd4f cold for stream rests on 4 samples. A fixed-host EC2 run (H1) would add nothing E4 needs: the cold effect is 4-9 s against a within-part round-to-round base spread of 0.2 s (0xd40) to 0.6 s (0xd0c).
